one_line_summary: Upright beach running stance showing functional sagittal mechanics with minimal forward lean.

findings.title: Head & Neck Position
findings.observation: Head remains upright with forward gaze and slight neck tension.
findings.tldr: Neutral gaze with minor neck tightness.
findings.eli5: Look straight ahead comfortably. Keep your neck relaxed.
findings.evidence: Cervical orientation influences vestibular stabilization and trunk alignment.

findings.title: Shoulder Carriage
findings.observation: Shoulders are slightly elevated and drawn back.
findings.eli5: Keep shoulders relaxed away from ears. High shoulders waste effort.
findings.evidence: Shoulder elevation raises upper-body tension and increases metabolic cost.

findings.title: Arm Swing
findings.observation: Arms flexed near 90 degrees oscillating primarily in sagittal plane.
findings.tldr: Functional arm swing tracking sagittal plane.
findings.eli5: Swing arms back and forth like pendulums. Avoid swinging across chest.
findings.evidence: Arm drive counterbalances torso rotational moments and optimizes cadence.

findings.title: Trunk & Forward Lean
findings.observation: Torso is overly upright with minimal forward lean from the ankles.
findings.eli5: Lean slightly forward from ankles like a ski jumper.
action: Cue slight forward tilt from ankles
findings.evidence: Ankle-derived lean utilizes gravitational torque to assist forward progression.

findings.title: Knee Mechanics
findings.observation: Stance knee flexes moderately under the body to absorb load.
findings.eli5: Bend knees softly upon landing like natural springs.
findings.evidence: Knee flexion during early stance attenuates vertical impact loading rates.

findings.title: Foot Strike & Overstride
findings.observation: Midfoot ground contact under yielding sand with a nearly vertical tibia.
findings.tldr: Foot lands close to center of mass.
findings.eli5: Step directly beneath yourself rather than reaching far out.
findings.evidence: Landing close to the center of mass minimizes braking impulse (Lieberman).

insufficient.title: Pelvic Stability & Hip Drop
insufficient.why: Frontal plane pelvic drop cannot be evaluated from a profile view.
